title: Life Experiences

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to share basic experiences and add a simple past detail. The central language is present perfect experience plus past simple detail. It belongs to the practical context of stories & experiences. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A2, connect the main message to a time, reason, contrast, or result. Listen for context before choosing the tense or functional phrase. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.text: present perfect experience plus past simple detail

blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the life experiences exchange.

blocks.english: I went there with my family last year.
blocks.explanation: This life experiences model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the life experiences exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “I've visited Canada twice.” and “I went there with my family last year.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled. Compare the time and viewpoint in each model, and use a linker when two ideas need a clear relationship. Avoid adding advanced forms when the lesson pattern already communicates the message accurately.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: present perfect experience plus past simple detail.
